items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: Well, my dad and my uncle. They was, you might say, my inspiration to start a musical career.

ctx.x: That must have had some music going on around there, some kind or another. Singing a music that you heard when you were young.

Well, my dad and my uncle. They was, you might say, my inspiration to start a musical career. What did they do? Well, they was tumblers, professional troopers traveling on the R.K. O. Sakers, you know, all over the country. See, they had acrobatic act. And of course my daddy, the final of the act would be my daddy would blow his trombone, and my uncle his trumpet and they'd play port and peasant, a duet, to close the act up after they got done tumbling. See, when the act was completed. They used that for final,…
Did they play alone or were the people in the pettacomps, or what?
